protocol: D-000 new cycle, turn 2 of 3; refute not confirm; verify C2-D047048-01 landed
summary: C2-D047048-01 is fully repaired and I proved the symmetry rather than eyeballing it: after normalising only the commit id, D-047's and D-048's Reversibility blocks are now byte-identical to each other, and both reproduce adopted D-028's wording including the after-dependents limb. I also proved the repair was surgical: both entries' decision blocks hash identically across turn 1 and turn 2 -- D-047 at 4b42d014e8e2ad3f and D-048 at 8d4811178d91675b -- so nothing outside the reversibility line moved. All four cited digests match live bytes, including my turn-1 verdict at 7a5182b5 characterized exactly as OBJECT with 1 SHOULD-FIX. Every remaining attack fails on clauses I verified at turn 1 and confirmed unchanged here. One note: the 're-measure at dispatch' parenthetical was dropped from the Measured-inputs header, which is the same drafting-aid drop I recorded against D-044 turn 2 and which I again measured as absent from every adopted entry.

notesRecorded.observation: Turn 1 read 'Measured inputs (re-measure at dispatch):'; turn 2 reads 'Measured inputs:'. The token-loss diff over the whole draft returns exactly three tokens -- 'dependents', 'dispatch', 're-measure' -- of which 'dependents' is the superseded phrase from the repair itself ('Total before dependents' becoming 'Total before any dependent disposition lands'), leaving the re-measurement parenthetical as the only real removal.
notesRecorded.whyItIsOnlyANote: I measured the same question I measured against D-044 turn 2 and got the same answer: 're-measure at dispatch' occurs zero times in adopted COORDINATOR-DECISIONS.md entries, so it is a drafting-stage instruction to the dispatch rather than content that reaches the register. Its function was discharged here -- I re-measured every cited input this turn -- and nothing had moved: COORD 37c375df and file 08 6547e6ac are identical to my turn-1 measurements, as is HEAD f6d9401.
notesRecorded.whyItIsWorthRecordingAtAll: This is the second entry in which the re-measurement aid has been silently dropped during an otherwise additive repair, and turn 3 plus adoption are still ahead. If a cited file moves before then, nothing in these bytes instructs anyone to re-measure. Restoring the parenthetical costs one line. Recorded for consistency with NOTE-C2-D044-T2-01 rather than as a new class of concern.

whatIVerified: Subject digest at start and end: cdc2a318ab57c2a73706f130b7d868094d9d6688b88803ef30661786309b8d2f both times, matching the dispatch. No drift.

The attack 'D-048 reversibility still missing the after-dependents limb' fails, and I tested it by comparison rather than by reading. Extracting both Reversibility blocks and normalising whitespace and the commit id, D-047's and D-048's are now string-identical: 'Total before any dependent disposition lands. After one lands, overturn also requires that disposition's owning-authority supersession.' Both reproduce adopted D-028's precedent wording, which was the standard I measured against at turn 1.

The repair is surgical, which matters because an additive fix should not disturb operative text. I hashed each entry's decision block from its '## D-04x' heading to its '### Reversibility' heading in both drafts: D-047 gives 4b42d014e8e2ad3f in turn 1 and turn 2, D-048 gives 8d4811178d91675b in both. Clauses 1 through 5 of each entry, the Subject lines, the owning-authority lines, the Alternatives and the Readiness lines are all untouched.
The token-loss diff over the whole draft returns three tokens and I traced every one to its source, rather than reporting a raw count. Nothing was lost from any decision clause.

The attack 'cited digests do not match live bytes' fails on all four: COORD 37c375df54b0cb652e9e6949aa27936462ce92ae7395b71b460d5c6d54acbfdf, file 08 6547e6ace2ae61e664af0f65059b66c2cb3d0539d64f6687aba04f8f54dc4cd7, Claude 2 turn 1 7a5182b5151aeafea9993dbc766c907773abddcc06443a1348ba2bc12bb00f5d, Codex turn 1 043f378eb290c24825f1b3a74ed4317f664562d85f5afaf9b4e9e0c8b18b3637. Each measured by me against live bytes.

My turn-1 verdict is characterized exactly as 'OBJECT, 1 SHOULD-FIX', which is what I returned -- verdict OBJECT, mustFix 0, shouldFix 1, notes 0, single id C2-D047048-01. The disposition table records it ACCEPTED with an accurate description, and records Codex's ADV-D048-T1-01 as the same repair, which is consistent with both of us having found the same defect.

The attack 'silent SATISFIED or condition-1 discharge' fails. SATISFIED appears only in refusals: the header's '**Does not** mark SATISFIED', each clause 5's 'Marks nothing SATISFIED', and each clause 4's 'A coordinator-composed SATISFIED is unlawful (DR-204)'. Condition 1 is never claimed discharged -- the construction stays conditional, future and row-scoped, 'A completed, reviewed, owner-recorded disposition may discharge condition 1 for DR-002 / DR-004 within the scope it names', which is adopted D-028's own construction.

The attack 'coordinator becomes recording authority' fails, and these entries remain stronger than the precedent on this axis: 'Coordinator selects. Named owners record. Coordinator may draft… D-000 does not make the coordinator the Evidence authority. Independent review is required. A coordinator-composed SATISFIED is unlawful (DR-204).' D-028 carries the first half of that and not the DR-204 sentence.

The attack 'unsverable bundle' fails. The header still declares 'Two severable entries', each entry retains its own Subject, owning authority, Decision, Alternatives, Readiness and Reversibility, the overturn commits remain distinct at C-D047 and C-D048, and D-047 still rejects 'Bundle with D-048 as one unsverable act. Rejected: D-025 defect.'

The attack 'condition 5 / docs/v2/implementation' fails: both clause 5s retain 'Conditions 2–5 remain. Condition 5 remains the only implementation authorization', and both retain 'Authorizes no blueprint'.

Nothing has been pre-applied: git reports the whole of docs/v2/architecture/ and COORDINATOR-DECISIONS.md clean, with zero modified tracked files. The environment is unchanged from turn 1 at HEAD f6d9401.

The two examined-and-declined items from turn 1 remain unchanged and I re-confirmed my reasoning holds: the clause-2 non-selection lists still omit DR-009 and DR-010, which is behind the categorical 'This selection is one row' and is an addition D-028 does not require; and D-048's alternatives still lack the reciprocal anti-bundling rejection, which one statement plus the header's severability declaration covers.
whatIDidNotCheck: The Codex turn-2 review of this subject. Not read; the file is confirmed absent at review time.

The Codex turn-1 verdict, hashed but never opened. The entry characterizes it as 'OBJECTIONS, 1 SHOULD-FIX' and records ADV-D048-T1-01 as accepted by the same repair. I verified the digest and not the class, the count, or that its finding was in fact the reversibility limb.

Adopted D-029 and D-030, cited in the header as form precedents alongside D-028. The measured-inputs table names D-028 as the form this pair copies, so I compared against D-028 in full at turn 1 and did not re-derive the other two.

Whether the owning authorities named for DR-002 and DR-004 are the owners file 08 currently records. I read the rows' status cells for standing at turn 1; I did not extract and compare the owner cells.

Whether Route B is the right preference for these rows. That is the PREFERENCE-LADEN judgement the entries exist to make; a refuting reviewer can test that the choice is disclosed, scoped and reversible, which it is.

environment.gitHeadSubject: DR-001: SATISFIED re-record after D-044 and MEASURED f6ad713
environment.note: The subject and review prompt are untracked working-tree files at review time; digests bind working-tree bytes, not committed objects. Recorded as a condition of review, not a finding, since the draft is pre-adoption and binds nothing.
environment.measurementTool: shasum -a 256; unified diff plus a python3 token-loss pass over the whole draft with each lost token traced to its source; python3 extraction of both Reversibility blocks with whitespace and commit-id normalisation to test symmetry by string equality; per-entry hashing of the decision blocks in both drafts to prove the repair was surgical; whitespace-normalised grep of COORDINATOR-DECISIONS.md to re-measure the re-measure convention; git status across docs/v2/architecture and COORD

consentNote: I CONSENT with zero MUST-FIX and zero SHOULD-FIX. My turn-1 objection was that two entries of the same class, drafted together, disagreed with each other about what an overturn requires once a dependent disposition exists. That is repaired, and I established it by string comparison of the two normalised blocks rather than by reading them as similar. I also checked the thing a repair most often gets wrong here: whether fixing one line disturbed anything else. It did not -- both decision blocks hash identically across the two turns. My single note is the dropped re-measurement parenthetical, graded consistently with the same drop I recorded on D-044 turn 2 after measuring that it never reaches an adopted entry.
